column1: # MUST_CONTAIN.tsv -- the BOM for v1.0.61.
# THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE. CM051 VENDORS IT.
# CM051 scripts/sync_cut_bom.sh copies this file into cuts/v1.0.61/ there and
# records the OS003 commit it came from in cuts/BOM_PIN. Authoring it in CM051
# instead produces a copy with no pin -- "a fork nobody declared". v1.0.61 saw
# that class TWICE in one hour: once in the v1.0.56 row's own words, and once
# live, when the v1.0.60 walk row was written on the VENDORED side and
# cut-gate-wrappers refused it. THE GATE READS THE TREE IT IS CUTTING.
# ⚠️ AND THE BOOTSTRAP IS UNREACHABLE BY ITS OWN REMEDY TEXT. sync_cut_bom.sh
# CANNOT-RUNs with "write it there first (bin/bom_add.sh)", and bom_add.sh
# exits 2 on a missing BOM -- so the remedy cannot create the file it demands.
# This header was written by hand for exactly that reason. Filed as CM051 #956.
# EVERY ROW SAYS ONE OF THREE THINGS AND NEVER A FOURTH
#   gate:<workflow>#<job>   a CI gate that FAILS on the real pre-fix tree
#   artefact:<sha8>#<what>  measured on the published artefact itself
#   needs-walk:<ver>#<what> UNPROVEN, and here is exactly what to look at
# `TBD` is not a state, it is a silence, and a silence is what turns into a
# surprise on a walk.
# TWO ROWS FOR NINE MERGES, AND THAT IS A STATEMENT NOT AN OVERSIGHT
# v1.0.61 carries nine merges. Only two are here, because a BOM row needs a
# capability_id that RESOLVES in manifest/capability_manifest.tsv AND a pattern
# that DISCRIMINATES -- present on the shipped tree, ABSENT on the pre-fix one.
# Both patterns below were mutation-tested against v1.0.60's CM051 pin before
# being written: post>0 AND pre=0, with OSTLER_EXTENSION_TOKEN (13/13) as the
# must-be-non-zero control proving the scan sees the tree at all. A pattern
# that scores non-zero on the pre-fix tree guards nothing; `failed_steps` was
# rejected on exactly that test (post=2, pre=1).
# The other seven merges are real and are recorded in cuts/v1.0.61/SCOPE.md.
# They are NOT given rows here rather than given rows that guard nothing.
what

🔴 A REUSE-SETTINGS RE-RUN SILENTLY DELETED THE CUSTOMER'S DAILY BRIEFS. Re-running the installer to change a setting takes SKIP_PHASE2, which leaves the Phase-2 channel defaults at CHANNEL_IMESSAGE_ENABLED=false with an empty allow-list; the assistant config is then regenerated wholesale, so the brief-channel resolver matched nothing and wrote ZERO [[cron.jobs]] entries. The customer's morning brief and evening wrap stopped, with no error and no prompt. The brief WRITER was never the defect. FIX (#1377): a fill-only restore reads the channel settings back out of the EXISTING config before regeneration, and restores each value ONLY where it is still at its Phase-2 default, so a deliberate later change is never overwritten. Proved by EXTRACTION and mutation, not by grep: the real pre-fix install.sh still fails arm A with 'wrote 0 [[cron.jobs]], expected 2 -- the customer lost their briefs'.

🔴 THE INSTALL CLAIMED A CLEAN FINISH OVER A FAILED STEP -- CAUGHT ON THE v1.0.60 ARTEFACT, NOT REASONED ABOUT. install.log's final line read 'DONE status=ok failed_steps=2 errors=0': the closing verdict consulted only _OSTLER_RUN_ERRORS, which counts err() MESSAGES and is blind to a STEP that ran and FAILED, so a hydrate step killed by its timeout raised no err() and a customer whose search index came out empty was told the install went fine. FIX (#1369): the verdict ALSO consults __OSTLER_FAILED_STEPS and NAMES the steps from __OSTLER_FAILED_STEP_IDS, appended at the one site that increments the count so the number and the names cannot disagree; the reassuring line prints only when BOTH tallies are zero. SCOPE, stated: this fixes the sentence a HUMAN reads. The DONE-marker status field a machine reads is sequenced separately and is NOT touched here.
